decision: Price and sell-through share one chart, with the agent forecast dashed after 'today'
why: The pricing decision is about the relationship between the two lines, not either one alone.
value: Cause, effect and forecast read in one glance; the chart draws once and then stays still.

decision: Product pages are static, revalidated on stock and price events
why: PDPs are read far more than they change; events tell the edge exactly when to refresh.
value: Fast pages for customers and no stale price after an approval.

decision: Stock by store × size as a heat grid, zeros in red
why: Size gaps in one store drive markdowns; a total hides them.
value: Merchandisers see whether a price problem is really a size problem.

decision: The pricing agent can only propose; a person approves
why: Price changes carry margin, brand and parity risk that sits with the owner.
value: Speed from the agent, accountability with the owner.

decision: Price rules are shown beside the decision and enforced by the same service
why: The UI and the agent must check the same guardrails, or approvals will fail late.
alternative: Keep rules in a separate admin area.
value: No surprises between what the screen allows and what the API accepts.
